annotations.description: GPT5m failed to respond to Emperor of Bones' Adapt 2 ability on the stack. Once Adapt resolves, Emperor gets +1/+1 counters which triggers reanimating the exiled Archon of Cruelty - a devastating 6/6 flyer whose ETB forces GPT5m to sacrifice a creature, discard a card, and lose 3 life while the opponent draws and gains 3 life. GPT5m had Solitude in hand with white cards (Prismatic Ending, Phlage) available to evoke, which would exile Emperor of Bones in response, preventing the entire sequence.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority, allowing Adapt 2 to resolve and Archon of Cruelty to be reanimated.
annotations.betterLine: Evoke Solitude by exiling Prismatic Ending (or Phlage) from hand, targeting Emperor of Bones. This exiles Emperor before Adapt resolves, preventing the +1/+1 counters and the Archon of Cruelty reanimation trigger entirely.

annotations.description: Discarded Solitude to Archon of Cruelty's trigger, losing premium instant-speed removal. Solitude can be evoked (exiling Phlage or Prismatic Ending) to exile Emperor of Bones, which is the engine repeatedly reanimating Archon of Cruelty each combat. Without Solitude, there's no clean answer to Emperor of Bones continuing to generate value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Solitude to Archon of Cruelty's forced discard trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Arena of Glory instead. It's the least impactful card in hand - it enters tapped (no Mountain in play), only produces red mana, and the player already has two fetch lands (Flooded Strand, Marsh Flats) for mana development. Keeping Solitude preserves the ability to evoke it to exile Emperor of Bones or future threats.

annotations.description: Timed out and passed priority in precombat main with Prismatic Ending available to exile Emperor of Bones (MV 2). Emperor of Bones has Archon of Cruelty in exile and will reanimate it at the beginning of opponent's next combat, which would be devastating (opponent draws, gains 3 life, forces sacrifice + discard + 3 life loss). At 11 life, GPT5m cannot afford to let Archon trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Crack Flooded Strand or Scalding Tarn for a land producing a second color, then cast Prismatic Ending for 2 colors (W + another) to exile Emperor of Bones (MV 2), preventing the Archon of Cruelty reanimation.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Prismatic Ending before cracking fetchlands to generate the necessary mana. The spell was rolled back because the player couldn't complete the mana payment. The correct sequence is to activate Flooded Strand and/or Scalding Tarn first to get mana-producing lands onto the battlefield, then cast Prismatic Ending targeting Emperor of Bones (which has Archon of Cruelty exiled under it and threatens to reanimate it).
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Prismatic Ending directly without first cracking fetchlands for mana-producing lands.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Flooded Strand and/or Scalding Tarn first to fetch lands that produce colored mana, then cast Prismatic Ending with X=2 (spending W + another color) to exile Emperor of Bones.

annotations.description: GPT5m Worrier timed out and failed to activate Flooded Strand, which was the only available action. Cracking Flooded Strand for a Watery Grave would have enabled casting Prismatic Ending with 2 colors of mana (W+U or W+B) to exile Emperor of Bones (MV 2), preventing the opponent from reanimating Archon of Cruelty next combat. Archon entering would force a sacrifice, discard, 3 life loss (to 7), while opponent draws and gains 3 life — a devastating swing that likely loses the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without activating Flooded Strand.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Flooded Strand to fetch Watery Grave (paying life to have it enter untapped), then cast Prismatic Ending for WU/WB to exile Emperor of Bones before combat.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Emperor of Bones (4/4) into an empty board when the opponent is at 10 life. The opponent has no untapped creatures to block. Dealing 4 damage would bring the opponent to 6 life, putting them in a very dangerous position with Psychic Frog coming online next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers, missing 4 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Emperor of Bones for 4 damage, bringing opponent to 6 life. There are no blockers and the pressure is critical at this life total.

annotations.description: Cast Phlage before playing a land drop. Arena of Glory would enter untapped (Sacred Foundry is a Mountain) and could be exerted for RR, giving 5 total mana instead of 3. This would allow casting Phlage while keeping mana open, or enable a larger Prismatic Ending to answer Emperor of Bones.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Phlage before playing a land, using all 3 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arena of Glory first (enters untapped due to Sacred Foundry being a Mountain), then cast Phlage with RW from Sacred Foundry + Plains and 1 from Hallowed Fountain, keeping Arena of Glory available or exerting it for extra mana/options.

annotations.description: At 5 life (going to 8 with Phlage's lifegain), GPT5m targeted the opponent's face instead of killing Psychic Frog. The opponent has 5 cards in hand and can discard to pump Psychic Frog and give it flying, easily swinging for lethal over Phlage. Going face to deal 3 to an opponent at 18 life is nearly meaningless compared to removing the immediate lethal threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted DSV3 Proud (opponent's face) with Phlage's 3 damage ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Target Psychic Frog with Phlage's 3 damage to kill it (1/2 creature dies to 3 damage), removing the threat that can fly over Phlage for lethal next turn

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with no creatures. Emperor of Bones is 4/4 and Psychic Frog is 1/2 (summoning sick). By discarding two cards to Psychic Frog now, it becomes 3/4, which combined with Emperor of Bones (4/4) represents exactly 7 damage = lethal next turn if unblocked. Passing without pumping misses setting up a potential lethal clock.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Psychic Frog's discard ability
annotations.betterLine: Discard two cards (e.g., duplicate Abhorrent Oculus and Unearth) to Psychic Frog to pump it to 3/4, setting up exactly lethal damage next turn (4+3=7) while also fueling graveyard for future Abhorrent Oculus casts

annotations.description: Exiled Quantum Riddler instead of Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury with Emperor of Bones' trigger. Phlage has Escape and the opponent has exactly enough cards in graveyard to fuel it. Leaving Phlage available means the opponent could escape it later for 3 damage + 3 life gain + a 6/6 flying body, which would be devastating given the close life totals.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Quantum Riddler from opponent's graveyard with Emperor of Bones' combat trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury to permanently remove the escape threat. This denies the opponent their most powerful graveyard recursion option.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with all lands tapped. Emperor of Bones is 4/4 and Psychic Frog is 1/2. By discarding 2 cards to Psychic Frog's ability (making it 3/4), attacking with both creatures would deal exactly 7 damage for lethal. Instead, the player passed priority without pumping the Frog.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Psychic Frog's discard ability to pump it.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Psychic Frog twice by discarding 2 cards (e.g., Gran-Gran and an Abhorrent Oculus) to make it 3/4, then attack with both Emperor of Bones (4/4) and Psychic Frog (3/4) for exactly 7 lethal damage against a tapped-out opponent.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with any creatures when the opponent is at 7 life with no blockers and all lands tapped. Emperor of Bones (4/4) + Psychic Frog (1/2) would deal 5 damage, putting the opponent to 2 life with no way to interact. Psychic Frog would also draw a card on damage. This was a timeout/no response, wasting a critical attack step.
annotations.actionTaken: No response - passed the declare attackers step without attacking, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Emperor of Bones and Psychic Frog for 5 damage (opponent to 2 life), plus draw a card from Psychic Frog's combat damage trigger. Lethal would be nearly guaranteed next turn.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with all lands tapped and no creatures on board. Emperor of Bones (4/4) + Psychic Frog pumped to 4/2 (discard 3 cards) = 8 damage, which is lethal. Even just attacking with both unmodified deals 5, putting opponent to 2. This was a timeout/no response that skipped the attack entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: No response — failed to declare any attackers, missing lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Emperor of Bones and Psychic Frog, discard 3 cards to pump Psychic Frog to 4/2, exile 3 cards from graveyard for flying if needed. 4+4=8 damage is lethal against 7 life with opponent completely tapped out and no blockers.

annotations.description: Missed lethal damage. Opponent is at 7 life with no blockers and all lands tapped. Emperor of Bones (4/4) + Psychic Frog (1/2) only deals 5, but discarding 2 cards to Psychic Frog's ability would pump it to 3/4, dealing exactly 7 = lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without pumping Psychic Frog, dealing only 5 damage instead of 7.
annotations.betterLine: Discard 2 cards (e.g., Abhorrent Oculus and Gran-Gran) to Psychic Frog to pump it to 3/4, dealing 4+3=7 damage for lethal.

annotations.description: At 2 life, the player chose Prismatic Ending over Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury. While Prismatic Ending exiles a threat, Phlage would deal 3 damage to remove a creature AND gain 3 life (going from 2 to 5 life), which is critical for survival. The life gain provides a much-needed buffer against the remaining threat. Phlage also goes to the graveyard, fueling a potential future escape.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Prismatic Ending to exile a creature
annotations.betterLine: Cast Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury to deal 3 damage to Emperor of Bones (or Psychic Frog) and gain 3 life, going from 2 to 5 life, then use remaining mana or next turn to address the other threat

annotations.description: At 2 life, activating Marsh Flats pays 1 life to go to 1, making them extremely vulnerable to any incidental damage. The opponent has 7 cards in hand and aggressive creatures. While fetching a land could be useful for future Quantum Riddler casting, the player already has 5 lands and can play Arena of Glory next turn for the 6th. There's no immediate need for the extra mana this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Marsh Flats in response to Phlage's trigger, going from 2 to 1 life
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let Phlage's trigger resolve (it's targeting Psychic Frog, not the player). Save the Marsh Flats activation for a time when the life point matters less or when Revolt is needed for Fatal Push.

annotations.description: Player timed out and failed to activate Marsh Flats while Phlage's trigger was on the stack. With Phlage about to gain 3 life (putting them to 5), spending 1 life on Marsh Flats to fetch a land would be safe and would give them a 6th land on the battlefield, helping cast Quantum Riddler (5 mana) next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not activate Marsh Flats
annotations.betterLine: Activate Marsh Flats to fetch a land (going to 1 life temporarily, then 4 after Phlage's +3 life), giving access to 6 lands for casting Quantum Riddler next turn.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 5 life with no creatures to block. Emperor of Bones attacks for 4 and Unearthing Psychic Frog from the graveyard (mana value 2) adds 1 power for exactly 5 damage = lethal. Psychic Frog could even be pumped by discarding cards if needed, but base stats alone are enough.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Unearth, missing lethal damage this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Unearth targeting Psychic Frog in graveyard for {B}, then attack with both Emperor of Bones (4/4) and Psychic Frog (1/2) for exactly 5 lethal damage.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Emperor of Bones (4/4) into an opponent at 5 life with zero blockers on board. This would have put the opponent to 1 life, making any subsequent attack or incidental damage lethal. The timeout/no response wasted a free 4 damage in a game where the opponent is already critically low.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Emperor of Bones for 4, putting the opponent to 1 life. Next turn's attack or any other source of damage would be lethal.

annotations.description: At 1 life facing a 4/4 Emperor of Bones, the player timed out and took no action. Quantum Riddler was listed as a castable spell, which would provide a 4/6 flying blocker and draw a card - essential for survival. Even if the full cast wasn't possible, playing a land and cracking Marsh Flats to develop mana was critical. Doing nothing at 1 life against a lethal attacker is game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority, taking no action in the main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Arid Mesa), crack Marsh Flats to fetch a blue dual land, then cast Quantum Riddler to get a 4/6 flying blocker and draw a card, which is the only realistic path to surviving another turn at 1 life.

annotations.description: At 1 life, Arid Mesa cannot be activated (costs 1 life to crack) and doesn't tap for mana on its own. It's a completely dead land drop. Arena of Glory would enter untapped (they control Mountains via Sacred Foundry and Thundering Falls) and provide an additional R mana, giving them 4 usable mana sources instead of 3.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Arid Mesa as land for turn, which is unusable at 1 life.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arena of Glory, which enters untapped and provides {R}, giving an extra mana source. While neither choice enables Quantum Riddler this turn, having access to more mana is strictly better than a dead fetchland.

annotations.description: Activating a fetch land at 1 life point costs 1 life, which kills them immediately (state-based actions check after resolution and they're at 0 life). There was no reason to sacrifice a fetch land here.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Marsh Flats at 1 life, paying 1 life to go to 0 and losing the game.
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate any fetch lands at 1 life. Pass priority and try to survive with the mana already available.

annotations.description: Activated Marsh Flats at 1 life, paying 1 life as part of the activation cost, which kills them immediately. At 1 HP, fetch lands that cost life cannot be activated without dying.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Marsh Flats (pay 1 life) while at 1 life, resulting in death.
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate Marsh Flats. Use existing untapped lands (Plains, Sacred Foundry, Thundering Falls, Arid Mesa) to cast spells. Could play Arena of Glory and potentially Warp a Quantum Riddler with available mana without paying any life.
